SQM / SOFTWARE QUALITY MONITOR

Turn a fixed bug
into a future check.

Manage safeguards based on incident records. Apply the relevant rules to your next change to find conditions that could repeat a problem.

  1. Past incident
  2. Safeguard
  3. Check the next change
When enabled, SQM checks within the scope of registered, applicable rules.

More detail, when you need it.

What can SQM check?+

SQM checks your changes against applicable safeguards registered from past incidents. Alongside the results, it identifies follow-up checks, such as testing the actual interface or verifying behavior after release.

Will it merge or release without me?+

Merge and release follow the permissions and approvals you have granted. Human blockers and repeated failures pause the work instead of triggering unlimited retries.

How thorough is the verification?+

Choose from five assurance levels according to the risk of the change. Level 5 is the most thorough. Every level preserves required checks and approvals.

5Maximum assuranceAuthentication, payments, sensitive data+

Check adjacent boundaries, failure, recovery and rollback. Independently review design, implementation boundaries and final results.

The broadest scope, with more preparation and verification.

4ProtectedPersistence, shared APIs, external effects+

Verify stored results, retries, idempotency and integration boundaries. Independently review design and final results.

More verification across shared boundaries and operations.

3BalancedDEFAULTNormal features and bug fixes+

Verify affected behavior, the main user journey and applicable static checks. Independently review the final candidate.

The default for bounded, reversible changes.

2FocusedSmall, isolated, reversible UI changes+

Verify the direct path and regression. Use independent review when repository policy or material uncertainty calls for it.

A narrower scope; not for changes to persistence or permissions.

1LightweightCopy, documentation and metadata+

Check the artifact, final diff and links. Preserve all repository-required checks and reviews.

For changes without runtime, data or security impact.

Duration depends on scope, environment, and approval waits.
